stem.en: In an FPTP election, Party A polled 40 per cent of the votes and won 60 per cent of the seats. What best explains this?

text.en: The votes must have been counted wrongly in some of the constituencies.
Party A came first in many constituencies, often below 50 per cent.
Seats were given to each party in proportion to the votes that it won.
The other parties' votes were removed from the count before the end.

explanation.en: Under FPTP, each constituency goes to the candidate with the most votes there. A party that comes first in many constituencies can win more seats than its vote share. No vote was lost or miscounted.

hints.en: Is the count done once for the whole country, or once in each constituency?
